plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray petals around a dark central disc packed with seeds. The heads track the sun when young, and the plant is grown widely for oil, seeds, and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, Argentina, and Europe
plants.funFact: The flower head is made up of hundreds to thousands of tiny individual florets arranged in a Fibonacci spiral pattern.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and slender spikes of small tubular flowers. Its blooms attract bees and butterflies and are harvested for essential oils, sachets, and cooking.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, with peak bloom from June to August, lingering into late summer in cooler regions
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and Tasmania
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie wildflower with drooping pink-purple petals around a spiky, copper-orange central cone. It is a favorite of pollinators and goldfinches, and is used in herbal remedies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (June to October)
plants.location: Native to the central and eastern United States prairies and open woodlands; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: A spectacular evergreen shrub with large, rounded crimson flower heads surrounded by showy bracts. It blooms in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter and early spring, and is the floral emblem of New South Wales.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (August to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the sandstone ridges and forests of southeastern Australia around Sydney and the Blue Mountains
plants.funFact: Each 'flower' is actually a dense cluster of hundreds of tiny individual flowers, and its nectar-rich blooms are pollinated mainly by honeyeater birds.
